text:
alex: quick heads up — seeing sawtooth-y latency spikes on prod dedicated pool when multivariant routing and continuous batching coincide. profiler shows jitter at kernel-select + kv-warmup boundaries.

mona: ugh. saw anything in the queue shape? like sudden tiny batches then a big one? :thinking_face:

alex: exactly that. queue size oscillates, batch coalescer flips between 3-5 requests and then a 20 req burst. spikes line up with model-compat fallbacks where variant A->B triggers kernel rebind.

javier: can you paste the perf snippet you mentioned?

alex: pasted below from pprof tail (trimmed):
```
CPU: 98% busy
time  ms | event
0.0-0.5 | kernel_select (A->B)  18%
0.5-1.2 | kv_warmup                26%
1.2-2.0 | batch_coalescer         12%
2.0-2.5 | kernel_launch            8%
... tail shows repeated kernel_select+kv_warmup bursts
```

sara: does this only happen on multi-model routes or also single-model with variant switching?

alex: mostly multi-model. single-model with small quant changes shows milder spikes but nothing like this.

infra-bot: deploy-bot noticed canary rollout on model-B-quant2 at 1813456000. Related? :robot_face:

mona: that might be it. if the routing policy falls back to model-B and the runtime decides kernel path B (different memory layout), the KV cache needs rekey/warmup which blocks coalescing.

javier: two angles: 1) change queue policy to prefer stable compatibility groups so bursts are grouped by compat-set. 2) reduce token_budget when a compat mismatch is predicted to avoid large batch formation until warmup done.

alex: tried a quick local patch that biases scheduler to hold batches for +6ms when compatness uncertain. reduced 95p latency from 420ms -> 230ms on replay. tradeoff: small increase in tail for steady-state single-variant traffic.

sara: can you share diff or pseudo-config? wanna test on dedicated-staging.

alex: config snippet i used:
```
scheduler:
  hold_on_compat_uncertain_ms: 6
  compat_threshold: 0.7  # probabilistic compat score from routing
  token_budget_target: 120  # lowered from 220 for uncertain batches
```

mona: lowering token_budget seems smart — fewer tokens per batch while KV warms up reduces kernel switching churn.

javier: watch out: too low token budget hurts throughput. we should auto-scale token_budget by measured warmup_duration: token_budget = baseline * exp(-warmup_sec/1.2)

sara: i'll run a canary with alex's config + kernel-select metrics enabled. can we add a histogram for kv_warmup duration and compat flips per 5m window?

alex: done. added histograms and an alert if kv_warmup 95p > 400ms for > 3m.

infra-bot: alert created: kv-warmup-95p-high on eng-runtime-dedicated

javier: next steps: (1) run canary on dedicated-staging for 2h (2) collect batch-shape, compat-flip counts, kernel-change events (3) evaluate throughput delta with token_budget autotune.

mona: also, profile kernel selection code path — maybe avoid full rebind if model weights compat enough. iirc we have a soft-path for kernel reuse that we can expand.

alex: noted. i'll push a small kernel-match tolerance patch and include microbenchmarks.

sara: assign owners? alex infra for scheduler change, mona for kernel-match, javier for token_budget autotune. i'll run canary and report back in 2h.

alex: thanks :thumbsup:

sara: any sign this caused customer impact? logs show a few 503s during spike windows but tied to overload protection kicking in.

alex: mitigation: temporary increase of dispatch concurrency + enable fallback to lower-capacity variant with warm cache. rolled that at 1813456500 and drop in 5xxs afterwards.

javier: good. let's reconvene after canary results and a short perf writeup.

sara: ack — will post summary thread with metrics.

alex: attaching replay id: replay-2026-04-12-77 for anyone who wants to reproduce.

mona: i'll start kernel-match PR now. tagging @javier for autotune algorithm review.

sara: thanks team — nice triage. :rocket:
